evidence.evidenceExists: Crash reports aggregated from the last 3 months show 47 incidents matching this pattern.
evidence.evidenceMissing: Stack traces are available but minimal repro steps were captured; we lack a deterministic reproducer.
assumptions: All 47 incidents share a common root cause, not multiple distinct bugs.
The crash reporter captures the full call stack without corruption.
evidence.uncertainty: Without a deterministic reproducer, we cannot confirm that a proposed fix will actually prevent recurrence.
evidence.disproofCriteria: If we find that the 47 incidents have at least 3 distinct root causes, the clustering assumption fails and we must split this artifact.

failureMining.failureObserved: Application crashes when rendering a table with more than 10,000 rows after a column sort.
failureMining.whereAppeared: Production dashboard view, observed across Chrome 120+ and Firefox 130+.
failureMining.likelyCause: Virtualized row recycling logic does not clean up sort-comparator references, causing use-after-free in the render cycle.
failureMining.competingExplanations: Memory pressure from large DOM subtrees; or a race between sort completion and the next render frame.
failureMining.biggestFailurePile: 47 crash reports in 3 months; 12 users reported the issue more than once.
failureMining.smallestNextFixOrTest: Write a minimal reproducer that creates 10,001 rows, triggers a column sort, and asserts no crash.
failureMining.whatNotToChangeYet: Do not rewrite the virtualized table component until the root cause is confirmed; a premature rewrite could mask the bug without fixing it.
failureMining.patternRecognition: Similar to a previously fixed crash in the tree-view component where event listener cleanup was incomplete.
